source_text:
Ὡς οὖν ἐσμὲν ἐπὶ γῆς, μετανοήσωμεν.
πηλὸς γάρ ἐσμεν εἰς τὴν χεῖρα τοῦ τεχνίτου: ὃν τρόπον γὰρ ὁ κεραμεύς, ἐὰν ποιῇ σκεῦος καὶ ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτοῦ διαστραφῇ ἣ συντριβῇ, πάλιν αὐτὸ ἀναπλάσσει, ἐὰν δὲ προφθάσῃ εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρὸς αὐτὸ βαλεῖν, οὐκέτι βοηθήσει αὐτῷ: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς, ἕως ἐσμὲν ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κόσμῳ, ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ἃ ἐπράξαμεν πονηρὰ μετανοήσωμεν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας, ἵνα σωθῶμεν ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ἕως ἔχομεν καιρὸν μετανοίας.
μετὰ γὰρ τὸ ἐξελθεῖν ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμον οὐκέτι δυνάμεθα ἐκεῖ ἐξομολογήσασθαι ἢ μετανοεῖν ἔτι.
ὥστε, ἀδελφοί, ποιήσαντες τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τὴν σάρκα ἁγνὴν τηρήσαντες καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ κυρίου φυλάξαντες ληψόμεθα ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
λέγει γὰρ ὁ κύριος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ: Εἰ τὸ μικρὸν οὐκ ἐτηρήσατε, τὸ μέγα τίς ὑμῖν δώσει; λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν.
ἆρα οὖν τοῦτο λέγει: τηρήσατε τὴν σάρκα ἁγνὴν καὶ τὴν σφραγῖδα ἄσπιλον, ἵνα τὴν αἰώνιον ζωὴν ἀπολάβωμεν.
thought_title: Repent while still in the world, as clay in the potter's hand
orientation: The preacher has just warned of the fate of those who corrupt the contest of incorruption, and now urges the congregation to repent while they are still on earth, before the time for repentance passes.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore we are on earth, let us repent. For we are clay in the hand of the craftsman: for in the way that the potter, if he makes a vessel and in his hands it is twisted or broken, again reshapes it, but if he gets ahead of it to throw it into the furnace of fire, no longer will he help it: so also we, while we are in this world, let us repent of the evil things we did in the flesh from the whole heart, so that we may be saved by the Lord, while we have time for repentance. For after we have gone out of the world, no longer can we confess there or repent still. So then, brothers and sisters, having done the will of the Father and having kept the flesh pure and having guarded the commandments of the Lord, we will receive eternal life. For the Lord says in the gospel: If you did not keep the small thing, who will give you the great thing? For I say to you, that the one faithful in the least is also faithful in much. So then he says this: keep the flesh pure and the seal spotless, so that we may receive back the eternal life.

choices.why: The image is of malleable material in the potter's hand; 'clay' preserves the craft metaphor exactly.
The term is generic for a skilled worker; 'craftsman' keeps the artisan sense without narrowing to potter, which is the specific example that follows.
The verb means to be distorted or warped while still in the hand, before firing; 'twisted' captures the deformation of wet clay.
The verb means to anticipate or act before something else happens; here the potter acts before the clay can be reshaped, so 'gets ahead of it' preserves the temporal urgency.
The verb means to acknowledge openly, here in the sense of confessing sins; 'confess' is the standard rendering and fits the context of repentance after death being impossible.
The compound verb means to receive what is due or what was promised; 'receive back' conveys the sense of getting the eternal life that was promised.

bible_refs.note: ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν
Εἰ τὸ μικρὸν οὐκ ἐτηρήσατε, τὸ μέγα τίς ὑμῖν δώσει; (cf. Luke 16:11-12, adapted)

pass_b_english: Since we are still on the earth, let us repent. For we are clay in the hand of the craftsman. Think of how a potter works. If a vessel he is making becomes twisted or broken in his hands, he reshapes it. But if he has already put it into the kiln, he can no longer help it. So it is with us. While we are in this world, let us repent from the whole heart of the evil things we have done in the flesh, so that the Lord may save us while we still have time for repentance. For after we have gone out of the world, we can no longer confess there or repent any longer.

So then, brothers, if we do the will of the Father and keep the flesh pure and guard the commandments of the Lord, we will receive eternal life. For the Lord says in the gospel: "If you did not keep what is small, who will give you what is great? For I tell you, the one who is faithful in the least is also faithful in much." This, then, is what he means: keep the flesh pure and the seal spotless, so that we may receive back eternal life.
